questions.prompt: The seven-function list used by the instructor includes _____ rather than motility as a named function.
questions.hint: Think about concentrating waste by removing water.
questions.explanation: Compaction is included in the lecture's list; motility describes mixing and propulsion.

questions.prompt: The soft mass of chewed food and saliva ready for swallowing is called a _____.
questions.hint: It is not yet the semifluid contents of the stomach.
questions.explanation: Chyme is formed after food mixes with gastric secretions.

questions.prompt: Synthesis of larger molecules from smaller building blocks is _____.
questions.hint: Contrast it with catabolism.
questions.explanation: Anabolism builds; catabolism breaks down.

questions.prompt: The movement of dissolved nutrient products across the gut epithelium into blood or lymph is _____.
questions.hint: This differs from enzymatically breaking food apart.
questions.explanation: Absorption is transport across a biological barrier.

questions.prompt: The enteric nerve network between the circular and longitudinal smooth-muscle layers is the _____ plexus.
questions.hint: The other major GI plexus lies in the submucosa.
questions.explanation: The myenteric (Auerbach) plexus chiefly coordinates motility.

questions.prompt: Alternating back-and-forth intestinal contractions that primarily mix chyme are called _____.
questions.hint: They are less propulsive than peristaltic waves.
questions.explanation: Segmentation helps expose chyme to the intestinal lining.

questions.prompt: The double peritoneal fold that supports abdominal organs and carries vessels is the _____.
questions.hint: It is a supporting membrane, not an epithelial surface.
questions.explanation: Mesenteries convey vascular, lymphatic, and neural structures.

questions.prompt: The outer connective-tissue layer that anchors much of the esophagus is called _____.
questions.hint: Compare this with a visceral peritoneal covering.
questions.explanation: The thoracic esophagus has adventitia rather than a full abdominal serosa.

questions.prompt: The salivary enzyme that starts starch digestion is _____.
questions.hint: It is not a protease or lipase.
questions.explanation: Salivary amylase acts on starch before food reaches the stomach.

questions.prompt: The parotid gland empties through _____ duct.
questions.hint: It is named after a historical anatomist, not Wharton.
questions.explanation: Stensen's duct carries parotid saliva into the oral vestibule.

questions.prompt: The duct of the submandibular salivary gland is _____ duct.
questions.hint: It is distinct from the parotid duct.
questions.explanation: Wharton's duct drains the submandibular gland.

questions.prompt: The small opening at the tip of a tooth root for neurovascular passage is the _____.
questions.hint: It connects with the root canal.
questions.explanation: Blood vessels and nerves enter at the root apex through the apical foramen.

questions.prompt: The anatomical name for the upper lip is the superior _____.
questions.hint: The lower lip is the inferior counterpart.
questions.explanation: The presentation explicitly uses superior/inferior labium for upper/lower lip.

questions.prompt: The voluntary first phase of deglutition is the _____ phase.
questions.hint: It uses the tongue to move the bolus posteriorly.
questions.explanation: Oral and buccal refer to the voluntary phase of swallowing.

questions.prompt: Swallowing reflex circuits are coordinated particularly in the _____.
questions.hint: This is a brainstem structure.
questions.explanation: The medulla helps integrate the pharyngeal and esophageal phases.

questions.prompt: The _____ esophageal sphincter helps prevent stomach acid from refluxing upward.
questions.hint: It is at the distal end of the esophagus.
questions.explanation: The lower esophageal high-pressure zone resists reflux.

questions.prompt: The opening in the diaphragm through which the esophagus passes is the esophageal _____.
questions.hint: It is not the aortic or caval opening.
questions.explanation: The esophageal hiatus permits the esophagus to enter the abdominal cavity.

questions.prompt: The gastric cells that make hydrochloric acid and intrinsic factor are _____ cells.
questions.hint: Chief cells have a different secretory role.
questions.explanation: Parietal cells are essential to gastric acidification and B12 absorption.

questions.prompt: The inactive protease precursor secreted by chief cells is _____.
questions.hint: Its active form has a shorter name.
questions.explanation: Acidic gastric conditions favor activation of pepsinogen to pepsin.

questions.prompt: The protein required for efficient ileal vitamin B12 uptake is _____.
questions.hint: It is produced by gastric parietal cells.
questions.explanation: Intrinsic factor travels with B12 to the terminal ileum.

questions.prompt: The expandable folds of the stomach lining are called _____.
questions.hint: They flatten when the stomach fills.
questions.explanation: Rugae permit expansion of gastric mucosa.

questions.prompt: The muscle controlling passage of chyme into the duodenum is the _____ sphincter.
questions.hint: It is the stomach's distal outlet regulator.
questions.explanation: The pyloric sphincter limits delivery of chyme into the duodenum.

questions.prompt: The phase triggered by food-related sights, smells, tastes, or thoughts is the _____ phase.
questions.hint: It begins before food reaches the stomach.
questions.explanation: The cephalic phase includes CNS-vagal stimulation.

questions.prompt: Stomach distension and peptides stimulate the _____ phase.
questions.hint: It takes place after food arrives in the stomach.
questions.explanation: Gastric-phase signals help stimulate acid, enzyme secretion, and mixing.

questions.prompt: Feedback that slows gastric activity when chyme reaches the small intestine is called _____ inhibition.
questions.hint: It protects the duodenum from being overloaded.
questions.explanation: Enterogastric inhibition restrains gastric secretion and emptying.

questions.prompt: Acid in the duodenum stimulates S cells to release _____.
questions.hint: It promotes pancreatic bicarbonate delivery.
questions.explanation: Secretin helps neutralize incoming gastric chyme.

questions.prompt: Fats and proteins in the small intestine stimulate I cells to release _____.
questions.hint: This hormone contracts the gallbladder.
questions.explanation: CCK coordinates pancreatic enzyme secretion and bile release.

questions.prompt: The inhibitory hormone produced by gastric D cells is _____.
questions.hint: It restrains gastrin and gastric acid secretion.
questions.explanation: Somatostatin provides inhibitory regulation of gastric function.

questions.prompt: The hormone released by intestinal K cells that promotes glucose-dependent insulin secretion is _____.
questions.hint: It is classified as an incretin.
questions.explanation: GIP contributes to post-meal insulin responses.

questions.prompt: The enteric signaling peptide prominently associated with intestinal vasodilation is _____.
questions.hint: Its name contains the phrase intestinal peptide.
questions.explanation: VIP supports vasodilation and intestinal secretion.

questions.prompt: The proximal small-intestinal segment receiving pancreatic secretion and bile is the _____.
questions.hint: It curves around the pancreatic head.
questions.explanation: The duodenum is the primary mixing region for chyme, bile, and pancreatic juice.

questions.prompt: The permanent circular intestinal folds are the plicae _____.
questions.hint: These folds are larger than villi.
questions.explanation: Plicae circulares are mucosal-submucosal structures expanding absorptive area.

questions.prompt: The lymphatic capillaries in intestinal villi that absorb chylomicrons are _____.
questions.hint: They are not ordinary blood capillaries.
questions.explanation: Long-chain lipids leave enterocytes as chylomicrons entering lacteals.

questions.prompt: The aggregated lymphoid nodules particularly prominent in the ileum are _____ patches.
questions.hint: Named lymphoid aggregates support immune surveillance.
questions.explanation: Peyer's patches are part of intestinal immune defense.

questions.prompt: The duodenal submucosal glands that secrete alkaline mucus are _____ glands.
questions.hint: They help protect the first small-intestinal segment from acid.
questions.explanation: Brunner's glands release protective alkaline mucus.

questions.prompt: The cells that line the small intestine and absorb most nutrients are called _____.
questions.hint: They have an apical brush border.
questions.explanation: Enterocytes are specialized intestinal absorptive epithelial cells.

questions.prompt: The pancreatic structures that synthesize exocrine digestive enzymes are the pancreatic _____.
questions.hint: Do not confuse them with endocrine islets.
questions.explanation: Acini drain their enzyme-rich secretions into a duct system.

questions.prompt: Pancreatic _____ helps raise the pH of acidic chyme in the duodenum.
questions.hint: The key product is a buffer rather than an enzyme.
questions.explanation: Duct cells secrete bicarbonate-rich fluid.

questions.prompt: The pancreatic enzyme primarily involved in triglyceride hydrolysis is pancreatic _____.
questions.hint: Amylase digests starch.
questions.explanation: Pancreatic lipase hydrolyzes dietary triglycerides.

questions.prompt: The main pancreatic duct is also called the duct of _____.
questions.hint: The accessory duct has a different eponym.
questions.explanation: The duct of Wirsung is the principal pancreatic drainage duct.

questions.prompt: The primary metabolic cells of the liver that also produce bile are _____.
questions.hint: They are distinct from resident liver macrophages.
questions.explanation: Hepatocytes synthesize bile and carry out major metabolic functions.

questions.prompt: Liver-resident macrophages situated in sinusoids are called _____ cells.
questions.hint: These cells are involved in immune surveillance.
questions.explanation: Kupffer cells are hepatic macrophages.

questions.prompt: The union of the right and left hepatic ducts produces the _____ hepatic duct.
questions.hint: It later meets the cystic duct.
questions.explanation: The common hepatic duct joins the cystic duct to form the common bile duct.

questions.prompt: The duct connecting the gallbladder to the extrahepatic bile system is the _____ duct.
questions.hint: The common bile duct forms after this duct joins the common hepatic duct.
questions.explanation: Gallbladder bile flows via the cystic duct.

questions.prompt: Most bile salts are reabsorbed in the terminal _____ before returning to the liver.
questions.hint: It is the last small-intestinal region.
questions.explanation: This is the intestinal recovery step of enterohepatic circulation.

questions.prompt: The sphincter controlling biliary and pancreatic flow at their duodenal entry is the sphincter of _____.
questions.hint: It surrounds the hepatopancreatic outflow.
questions.explanation: The sphincter of Oddi regulates bile and pancreatic secretion delivery.

questions.prompt: The round ligament of the liver is a remnant of the fetal _____ vein.
questions.hint: It carried placental blood before birth.
questions.explanation: The ligamentum teres is associated with the fetal umbilical vein.

questions.prompt: The saclike pouches visible along much of the colon are called _____.
questions.hint: They are not intestinal villi.
questions.explanation: Haustra contribute to the characteristic segmented appearance of the colon.

questions.prompt: The longitudinal smooth-muscle bands of the colon are the taeniae _____.
questions.hint: There are usually three bands.
questions.explanation: Taeniae coli contribute to formation of the haustra.

questions.prompt: The colonic bend adjacent to the liver is the _____ flexure.
questions.hint: The other major flexure lies near the spleen.
questions.explanation: The hepatic flexure lies between ascending and transverse colon.

questions.prompt: The smooth-muscle anal sphincter under involuntary control is the _____ anal sphincter.
questions.hint: Its partner is skeletal muscle under voluntary control.
questions.explanation: The internal anal sphincter relaxes reflexively during defecation.

questions.prompt: The gut-derived fermentation products acetate, propionate, and butyrate are short-chain _____ acids.
questions.hint: They are abbreviated SCFAs.
questions.explanation: These are microbial fermentation products absorbed in the colon.

questions.prompt: Inflammation of the pancreas is called _____.
questions.hint: Gallstones can trigger it by blocking drainage.
questions.explanation: Pancreatitis may follow biliary obstruction or other insults.

questions.prompt: Yellowing of the skin and sclera from accumulated bilirubin is called _____.
questions.hint: It is a clinical finding, not a specific etiology.
questions.explanation: Jaundice accompanies elevated bilirubin.

questions.prompt: Advanced, chronic liver scarring is called _____.
questions.hint: It is not simply acute hepatitis.
questions.explanation: Cirrhosis involves fibrosis and altered liver architecture.
